shortName: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: Thirty credits are the minimum credit requirements; courses from biology, chemistry, physics, or math-based disciplines are expected to constitute these 30 credits. We recommend anatomy, physiology, and genetics courses to ensure the best alignment with first-year classes in our program. We strongly encourage more than 30 credits to be applied and to trend toward upper-level courses in basic science over a steady program of courses.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Stritch School of Medicine is dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive community that upholds access, equity, and excellence as core values. We believe that diversity is integral to our mission of transformative education, innovative discovery, and service to others. We are committed to achieving excellence by utilizing the rich talents of people who infuse different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences into the work and learning environment and reflect the diversity of the populations whose health we hope to impact. As such, we embrace a broad spectrum of human expression and characteristics that includes but is not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, socioeconomic status, disability, sexual orientation, religion, military or veteran status, and age. Our diversity programming can be viewed on our website at https://ssom.luc.edu/diversity/programs/.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may be approved for a leave of absence (LOA) due to documented health problems, or personal tragedy, or to pursue an educational or research experience outside of the standard medical school curriculum. LOA's for other purposes are reviewed on a case-by-case basis. LOA's should be approved in advance of the starting date and typically may not exceed one calendar year in length; successive one-year leaves may be granted to permit completion of educational requirements, such as the MD/PhD degree program.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: At the Stritch School of Medicine, we want our students to have a life beyond the classroom so that their educational experience includes personal and academic growth. That's why we encourage participation in campus organizations, medical school committees, community service opportunities, faith-building activities, and other extracurricular pursuits. Stritch students are enriched by their involvement in professional, service, or recreational interest groups. They can participate in various extracurricular community service opportunities sponsored by Student Affairs, University Ministry, the academic deans' offices, and Loyola-supported student organizations. Students enjoy spending some relaxation time at the Loyola University Center for Fitness, a 62,000- square-foot facility adjacent to the medical school. The center offers exceptional amenities, and Medical students are automatic members by paying a student fee.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: We are located directly west of Chicago in Maywood, IL. Our campus is adjacent to Hines Veteran's Administration Hospital, one of the largest VA Medical Centers in the United States.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Nearby city and suburb areas provide plenty of housing options for students. There is no campus housing.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Our Jesuit tradition calls all faculty, students, and staff to intentionally honor the dignity of all persons and promote social justice. To that end, we aim to value the contribution of all individuals and create an environment that inspires a cadre of talented people to become leaders in science and medicine. By fostering a vibrant and dynamic culture of inclusion, the Stritch School of Medicine will continue to welcome opportunities to address challenges in health care and excel in academic medicine. At Stritch, we advocate for and support the interests of student affinity groups, not limited to but including students of color, those under-represented in medicine (UIM), LGBTQ students, veterans, first-generation and low-income students, as well as students with differing abilities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
SSOM provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities who apply for admission to the MD degree program and who are enrolled as medical students. It is the responsibility of a candidate with a disability, or a candidate who develops a disability, who requires accommodations to meet technical standards, to self-disclose to the accessibility office and request accommodations. All requests for accommodations are reviewed on an individualized, case by case basis. It is the mission of the accessibility office to uphold the university's commitment to legal (ADA) compliance and educational integrity through an interactive process.
All students, regardless of disability, are offered academic support and resources provided through the academic center, including access to peer tutors and mentors, books and study aids, individual advising and USMLE board preparation support.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Stritch physicians-in-training learn how to care for the health and well-being of others.  It's also important to understand and attend to your health and well-being as a physician-in-training during your training. In January 2023, the Health Sciences Campus opened a Wellness Center to provide students with programs and services geared to physical, emotional, and overall well-being.  

WELLNESS IS MULTI-FACETED from personal to spiritual, academic, financial, and environmental health.  Through the Wellness Center, Ministry, ACE, the Student Wellness Committee, and other resources, Stritch is dedicated to helping each physician-in-training reach their full potential while providing support to help them care for themselves, each other, and the broader patient populations and communities they serve. Resources for wellness at the Stritch School of Medicine are at the following URL.
https://www.luc.edu/stritch/studentlife/wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine (SSOM) has a campus culture emphasizing community building, diversity, and inclusion. The school's student life program focuses on community building and informal learning. SSOM's core values encourage a community formed of diverse backgrounds, beliefs, and experiences to collaborate in an inclusive environment that emphasizes care for others (Cura Personalis). SSOM aims to create a vibrant and dynamic community culture that supports students regardless of their race, ethnicity, beliefs, income level, gender, sexual orientation, and more. SSOM is one of four medical schools in the United States rooted in Jesuit Catholic values. Jesuit values are central to the school's curriculum, how faculty teach, and how students learn. SSOM prepares students to act with humility and curiosity as they care, teach, learn, and lead in dynamic community contexts across the globe.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Ultimately, students need to be able to travel to/from school, and later in their M3/M4 years to their clerkship rotation sites. In almost all instances, students should have a driver’s license and car in order to get to their destinations. Otherwise, they need some other mode of transportation (e.g. public transportation, ride share), and they may be less convenient, more time consuming, or more costly.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to be in compliance with the appearance and uniforms standards of the Stritch School of Medicine, which are in accord with the uniform policy of Loyola University Medical Center.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Academic Center for Excellence (ACE) is a learner-centered service designed to support the ongoing academic development and life long learning of the adult learner in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students gain early clinical exposure through physician- and peer-mentor programs and student organizations that affiliate with local free and reduced-cost clinics.

medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures are currently asynchronous, while small groups are mandatory to attend.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The first year of the curriculum concentrates on the fundamental scientific principles and processes related to the human body's standard structure, function, and regulation. First-year students also receive instruction in human behavioral science, communication and medical interviewing skills, the doctor/patient relationship, health promotion/disease prevention, professionalism, medical ethics, and healthcare's social and community context. The second year focuses on basic science principles related to the mechanisms of human disease, pharmacology, and the therapeutic approach to disease. Students develop their basic clinical skills by gaining experience in physical examination, effective history-taking, and evidence-based clinical decision-making. The third and fourth years are organized into eight required clinical clerkships, two medicine sub-internship experiences, and up to 34 weeks of elective time chosen from a catalog of over 100 clinical electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students receive instruction in business and leadership skills, inter-professional interactions, justice in health care, disaster preparedness, nutrition, end-of-life issues, patient safety, global health, and healthcare delivery. Special curricular features include an emphasis on bioethics, professionalism, communication, and intensive training in history-taking and the physical examination. Students also benefit from the availability of advanced medical simulation models located in the Clinical Skills and Human Simulation Centers that provide the latest educational and simulation technology and offer ample opportunities to develop clinical skills further.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Loyola University Chicago, founded in 1870 by the Jesuits, is one of the largest Catholic universities in the United States. By 1909, the university had organized several small medical colleges into a new medical school, and, in 1948, the school was named in honor of Samuel Cardinal Stritch, Archbishop of Chicago. In 1969 the University opened the Loyola University Med. Center, built on land given by the Veterans Administration, in Maywood, a suburban community located 12 miles west of downtown Chicago. In 2011, Loyola transferred its clinical and patient care operations to Trinity Health, one of the largest Catholic health systems in the United States, and established a new Health Sciences Division to enhance the University's academic and research enterprise at the medical center campus. The campus's prominent buildings include Stritch School of Medicine, Marcella Niehoff  School of Nursing, Loyola Center for Fitness, Cardinal Bernardin Cancer Center, and Loyola University Hospital.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine (SSOM) is committed to scholarship and the education of medical professionals and biomedical scientists. Our school, including its faculty, trainees, and staff are, called to go beyond facts, experimentation, and treatment of disease to prepare people to lead extraordinary lives and treat the human spirit in an environment that encourages innovation embraces diversity, respects life, and values human dignity.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks are provided for candidate to complete a Declaration of Intent once accept offer is made. This holds the seat, without deposit, until final decision is made to CTE.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Please visit our website for additional details about letters of recommendation at http://ssom.luc.edu/admission/applying-to-stritch/
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: At least two letters should be from science faculty affiliated with your undergraduate or graduate academic program. We strongly recommend at least one letter come from an M.D.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Candidates will select an in-person or virtual interview day when invited to interview. All interview days include a 45-minute orientation, one full file and one partial file interview with members of our admissions committee, and a 30-minute wrap-up/Q & A session.  In-person interview days will begin at 9:00 AM (CST) and end by 3:30 PM. In-person interview days include lunch and panel discussions with students and staff and campus and hospital tours. 
Virtual interview days will begin at 11:00 AM (CST) and end by 3:30 PM. Virtual interview days include a virtual chat with current students and pre-recorded content on our program and curricular options. All invited candidates are expected to participate in virtual and in-person interviews throughout the entire interview day. We will include instructions and recommendations for virtual interview preparation in your invitation.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: For Cycle 2026, candidates can choose between in-person and virtual interviews. The admissions committee will conduct one full file and one partial file interview.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Regional candidates are encouraged to visit in person if possible.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: In-person and virtual interviews are provided until further notice. VITA will not be used.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: All eligible candidates must be either US Citizens, DACA recipients in active standing or those who hold Permanent Resident status. Candidates are accepted both as in-state and out-of-state residents.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: There are no state residency requirements for application to Stritch.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: We are a private institution and accept applications from any state without quotas.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian applicants must be either permanent residents in the U.S. or have dual citizenship in U.S.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Permanent residents, adjusted statuses, and asylee/refugee statuses are considered on a case by case basis in our pool.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine (SSOM) seeks to recruit and enroll students in complete alignment with our Jesuit values: care for the whole person, education in the service of social justice, and reverence & respect for the community.  We seek academically prepared candidates with significant and sustained:
* service and community engagement
* academic preparation, achievement, and curiosity
* leadership and inspiration/agency for change
* commitment and personal ethic for social justice & service, specifically to the underserved

SSOM carefully reviews criminal histories, institutional actions, behavioral records, and matters of public record submitted by applicants through the AMCAS application, supplemental application, and securely transmitted letters of recommendation. SSOM will consider deferment requests from candidates holding acceptances from May 1 to June 15, 2026. No deferment requests will be considered beyond June 15. Deferment requests require a formal request to the Dean of Admissions and consideration by the Executive Committee on Admissions.

SSOM requires that all applicants who apply consecutively for the third time (or more) petition the Admissions Office to have their new application considered. This policy defines an application as a verified application submitted through AMCAS and sent to SSOM via AMCAS in three or more consecutive cycles. Petitions are considered only when candidates upload the document through the SSOM applicant portal (no other petitions will be accepted). Please title the uploaded document 'Petition for Admissions' when providing this information to the committee via your portal.

**Additional notes:
•	MCAT- During the 2027 application cycle, we will accept MCAT scores for exams taken after January 2024. Canceled test administrations may cause you to submit your application later than intended. All applications submitted before the December 11, 2026 deadline will receive full consideration. As in previous cycles, you may submit your primary and secondary applications before taking the MCAT. Suppose you have indicated on your primary application that you are registered for an upcoming MCAT date in 2026. In that case, a review of your completed application will not begin until your most recent MCAT score is received. Alternatively, you may wait until you receive your score before submitting your application as long as you submit your secondary application before December 11, 2026. 
•	Letters of Evaluation - no policy changes.
•	Interviews - All candidate interviews will be able to select a live or virtual interview option for the 2026 admissions cycle unless otherwise informed. Live interviews will require proof of vaccination before the visit. We will not need or use the VITA or other asynchronous interview platforms during this cycle.
•    We are encouraged to get to know you personally through your application material; as a result, there will be no support for AI-generated applicant responses within any part of your submitted application (primary or secondary).
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are considered holistically, and other academic details and metrics are provided in the AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: The committee preferences subsection scores that meet or exceed 50% (125) in CPBS and BBFL within your most recent MCAT exam. The committee favors candidates who have succeeded on their initial MCAT. Those with multiple MCAT scores will require further review of academic coursework and results.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: The committee preferences upward trending within the candidate's total academic progression, including postbacc and graduate programs.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Holistic review is used to consider trends and details within the coursework when making decisions about candidates with post bacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Our process considers at least 24 credits in a post bacc or graduate program to be a reasonable trend to correlate with undergraduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Although the committee considers community college credits within the academic review, these credits cannot be used to fulfill required pre-requisite coursework.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We recommend that candidates provide updates that help us understand their progress in professional, academic, or personal growth during the cycle.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The MD degree represents broad, undifferentiated training that affirms a student’s general medical knowledge and the essential physical, cognitive, emotional, and behavioral abilities needed for medical practice. At the Stritch School of Medicine (SSOM), students are expected to complete all components of the curriculum and participate fully in medical training. SSOM prepares graduates to be competent, compassionate physicians who qualify for residency and medical licensure. Rooted in the Jesuit tradition, SSOM emphasizes rigorous academics, personal growth, and service to others. To meet its responsibility to society, SSOM requires students to demonstrate strong judgment, comprehensive knowledge, and refined technical skills. These expectations—known as technical standards—include abilities in observation, communication, motor function, intellectual and quantitative skills, and social and behavioral functioning.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: All financial assistance available is determined by filling out the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Once the FAFSA data has been received by the school (from the Department of Education), you will be awarded aid in the form of Direct Federal Stafford Loans. Institutional scholarships and grants may also be available. This aid is based on financial need and is determined by the economic data entered on the FAFSA (by both students and parents). Applicants will receive an estimated award letter before April 30th.

medSchoolPrograms.info: ASPIRE is an intensive pre-medical program held during the month of June, designed to prepare you to successfully navigate the medical school application process.  Our curriculum will help you strengthen your application, deepen your understanding of health disparities, build your capacity for health equity leadership, and introduce you to the community of Maywood, IL.

The dual MD/MPH degree program is competitive and limited to 10 students per academic year. Applicants must meet the following criteria:
Admission to the Stritch School of Medicine (through AMCAS)
Completion of the MD/MPH application through the Loyola University Chicago online application system
Statement of Purpose for our MPH Program
Submission of official undergraduate transcripts to Loyola University Chicago's Office of Graduate and Professional Enrollment Management (GPEM)
No GRE required
Application deadline: April 30 to ensure an M0 start.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Application review will begin July 7, 2025, for all candidates with submitted and verified AMCAS primary and completed/submitted supplemental applications. Reviews are conducted on a first-come, first-served basis.
Interviews for the 2025 cycle will begin on this date.
AMCAS primary applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 PM (CST) on this date to be considered for the 2026 cycle.
Secondary application must be submitted by 11:59 PM (CST) on this date.
If applying to our MD/PhD program, please note that the CTE deadline is April 30, 2026.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: It is typical for about 50 candidates to be placed on the waitlist after May 15th.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Candidates in continued consideration, post interview, are given the option to opt-out of being placed on the waitlist which is constituted in mid-May.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants who present academic credentials that indicate they are capable of succeeding in the rigorous medical education program will be evaluated for evidence of the personal qualifications they can bring to the medical profession. Essential characteristics include an interest in learning, integrity, compassion, and the ability to assume responsibility. Of particular interest will be an applicant's exploration of medicine and the nature of their motivation to enter the medical profession. Early submission of the AMCAS application and prompt return of all supporting material will enhance an applicant's chance of being offered an interview. Loyola University does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Committee preference given to progressive rigor and academic progress in chemistry and biology courses within three years of desired matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: A bachelor's degree and an MCAT taken no later than November of the year of application, are required. Any undergraduate major is acceptable. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, hold a permanent resident visa, or be eligible for the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA)* process of the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services at the time of application. Applicants enrolled in advanced degree programs must expect to complete their degrees prior to matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is strongly encouraged. Clinical exposures involving active participation from candidate are also strongly encouraged.
